newsitem.title: FRANCE: French president says economic reforms going well.
newsitem.headline: French president says economic reforms going well.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac told the cabinet on Wednesday that economic, defence and education reforms were on track and urged ministers to stay the course.

"The current always runs strongest when you get to the middle of the river. We cannot turn around because that would be a step backwards," Chirac told a regular weekly cabinet meeting, according to government spokesman Alain Lamassoure.
"The president noted that overall, reforms were going ahead in a satisfactory manner -- in defence, education and soon in the budget," Lamassoure told reporters after the meeting.
The National Assembly's finance committee took up the government's proposed 1997 budget on Thursday, and the assembly itself is to debate the plan from October 15.

The government's programme of fiscal austerity, intended to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999, has been unpopular with voters and deputies alike during a time of record unemployment.

Embattled French Prime Minister Alain Juppe, who has predicted an economic upturn in 1997, won a lukewarm vote of confidence from the Senate on Tuesday after reaffirming he wanted to step up the battle for jobs.
Senators voted by 219 to 94 to endorse Juppe in a confidence motion mirroring an unenthusiastic vote last week by the National Assembly, the lower house of parliament.
Juppe sought the votes as a way of uniting his fractious centre-right coalition behind him at a time opinion polls show his popularity at a record low.
